zh: 我认为这里有一个类比，你知道的，当云计算变得——你知道的——我猜是变得流行或日益普及时，存在一个相对的区间，你知道的，有些公司立刻就领悟了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And used it very efficiently.
zh: 并且非常高效地使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are companies that are still trying to migrate from on-prem to cloud.
zh: 还有一些公司仍在尝试从本地部署（on-prem）迁移到云。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think incidentally, I think AI is pushing a lot of people now, like the ones that were sort of procrastinated on it.
zh: 而且我认为顺便说一下，我认为 AI 现在正在推动很多人——比如那些之前一直拖延的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can sort of imagine, right, that there are a lot of people that are kind of procrastinating on how agentic they're becoming.
zh: 你可以想象，对吧，有很多人在如何变得更具智能体化（agentic）这件事上有点拖延。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're probably going to get lapped by these organizations that are moving more autonomously and with more conviction.
zh: 而他们很可能会被这些更自主、更有信念地行动的组织套圈。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's go deeper on that.
zh: 那么让我们深入探讨一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: What separates the company that really squeezes AI to the fullest?
zh: 是什么把真正把 AI 榨取到极致的公司区分开来？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it building the autonomous software factories?
zh: 是构建自主的软件工厂吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this changes every quarter.
zh: 因为这每个季度都在变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really think we have a once in a lifetime opportunity.
zh: 我真的认为我们有一个千载难逢的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: to do what customers want, which is sort of ironic to say, but like any big company at any given time is getting customer feedback.
zh: 去做客户想要的，这么说有点讽刺，但任何大公司在任何给定时刻都在获取客户反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, let's say you're Comcast, right?
zh: 你知道的，假设你是 Comcast，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like people are saying things on Reddit, they're calling your call center, they're, you know, sending you emails and their internet broke down and they want to understand why.
zh: 比如人们在 Reddit 上发表评论，他们打你的客服电话，他们，你知道的，给你发邮件，他们的网络断了，他们想了解原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your ability today to turn those detractors into net promoters?
zh: 你今天有什么能力能把这些批评者（detractors）转化为净推荐者（net promoters）？

speaker: Unknown
en: When they're reaching out, are you responding with a high-quality agentic response?
zh: 当他们联系过来时，你是否在用高质量的智能体回复来回应？

speaker: Unknown
en: When they reach out to report a problem, are you kicking off an incident investigation?
zh: 当他们联系过来报告一个问题时，你是否在启动一次事故调查？

speaker: Unknown
en: When they're reporting with a very concrete, fixable thing, are you fixing it autonomously?
zh: 当他们报告一个非常具体的、可修复的问题时，你是否在自主地修复它？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is actually a pretty decent way to grade a rubric for how agentic are you.
zh: 我认为这其实是一个相当不错的评分标准（rubric），用来衡量你有多智能体化。

speaker: Unknown
en: From customer signal that is decisive about something in your product being broken, defective, or in need of improvement, are you actually shipping that?
zh: 从「客户信号明确指出你的产品中某些东西坏了、有缺陷或需要改进」开始，你是否真的在交付那个修复？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you shipping the fix for that signal, the thing that addresses that signal?
zh: 你是否在针对那个信号交付修复，那个解决该信号的东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what is your latency?
zh: 你的延迟是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you could almost make a case that you can measure this sort of like mathematically, right?
zh: 比如，你几乎可以论证说你可以用类似数学的方式来衡量这个，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, okay, signal came in, eventually you're gonna get to fixing it.
zh: 比如，好，信号进来了，最终你会去修复它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe to give you sort of a lay of the land, there's the company that periodically scrubs that, maybe through taste, maybe with product managers, maybe by, you know, getting enough escalations, they're like, ah, I'm going to fix it.
zh: 也许为了给你一个大致的全景，有一种公司会周期性地清理那些信号，也许凭品味（taste），也许通过产品经理，也许通过，你知道的，积累足够多的升级（escalations），然后说：啊，我要修复它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's the company that is sort of like becoming truly more autonomous in a good way, right?
zh: 还有一种公司则是在真正变得更自主，而且是好的意义上的自主，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not in the sense of like, we let the agents go crazy and ship slop.
zh: 不是那种「我们放任智能体乱来并交付垃圾（slop）」意义上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, speaking of JEV and why people are so excited about it, you know, this idea of, like, really fast decision making can be super critical in shaping these software factories.
zh: 而且，你知道的，说到 JEV 以及人们为什么对它如此兴奋，你知道的，这种真正快速决策的理念，在塑造这些软件工厂方面可能极其关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because I'm mentioning that there is an element of judgment and taste also in, you know, famously folks like Steve Jobs, EHH, and many others have said, you know, like, you're not just a machine that turns whatever customers want into product.
zh: 因为我在说，这里面有判断力和品味的成分，你知道的， famously 诸如 Steve Jobs、EHH 等许多人都说过，你知道的，比如，你不只是一台把客户想要的任何东西变成产品的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is an element of decision making there, but there's also an objectivity to like, you know, your product might be erroring.
zh: 这其中有决策的成分,但也有一种客观性,比如说,你知道的,你的产品可能正在报错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's, you know, throwing up a bunch of exceptions in prod or someone comes in with a legitimate, very straightforward improvement.
zh: 所以,你知道的,它在生产环境里抛出一堆异常,或者有人带着一个合理的、非常直接的改进建议找上门来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we like to do this a lot on X, like when people like give us feedback on X.
zh: 你知道的,我们在 X 上很喜欢做这种事,比如人们在 X 上给我们反馈的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes they attach a screenshot or a video and it's like, that's spot on.
zh: 有时他们会附上一张截图或一段视频,然后就会觉得,这说得太准了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no human creativity involved here.
zh: 这里不涉及任何人类的创造力。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're pointing out something that they experienced and it was a problem that we should fix it right away.
zh: 他们在指出他们亲身经历的事情,那是一个我们应该立刻修复的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's kind of like an opportunity to test out this software factory hypothesis.
zh: 所以这有点像是一个检验这个软件工厂假设的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interestingly, yesterday we got a guy saying that he was getting confused by our navigation.
zh: 有意思的是,昨天我们收到一个人说,他被我们的导航搞糊涂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he gave me some really good feedback, but nothing that was like immediately actionable.
zh: 他给了我一些非常好的反馈,但没有什么是可以立即执行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like it's not like I could take his thing and turn it into a prompt.
zh: 就是说我没法把他的东西直接拿过来变成一个提示词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we did is the leader of our sort of like dashboard product area reached out to this gentleman and they started going back and forth.
zh: 所以我们做的是,我们负责仪表盘产品领域的负责人联系了这位先生,他们开始来回沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: He gave us more videos.
zh: 他给了我们更多视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: He gave us more qualitative feedback.
zh: 他给了我们更多定性反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even then requires another layer of human judgment to turn it into a decision for what we're going to do with the product.
zh: 而即便如此,还需要另一层人类判断,才能把它转化为我们要对这个产品做什么的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, one could project very far out in the future, which in AI could be six months, 12 months.
zh: 现在,人们可以往很远的未来去投射,在 AI 领域那可能就是六个月、十二个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a world where some of that UI and some of that expectation that this customer have, that would become their own generative interface.
zh: 存在这样一种世界:其中一些 UI 以及这位客户的一些期望,会变成他们自己的生成式界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we're a ways away from that.
zh: 但我认为我们离那还有一段距离。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, it's still our role to sort of like balance out feedback that we get from customers and then sort of eventually find its way into a prompt and eventually find its way into a shipped product.
zh: 所以,你知道的,平衡我们从客户那里收到的反馈、然后让它最终进入一个提示词、最终进入一个已上线的产品,这仍然是我们扮演的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when it comes to like the obvious ones, like button isn't working, payments are failing.
zh: 那么说到那些明显的情况,比如按钮坏了、支付失败了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the number of like, like you said, the latency towards a fixed resolution?
zh: 你觉得这个数量,就像你说的,朝着修复解决的方向的延迟?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Resolution, is that like one of the main numbers of predicting of a business success?
zh: 解决,这是不是预测商业成功的主要指标之一?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if you go from first principles, business is a product that gets better over time.
zh: 因为如果你从第一性原理出发,商业就是一个随时间变得更好的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unless you have a super small addressable market, it's like that business that can just fix everything in sub 30 minutes is going to destroy a business that takes two days.
zh: 除非你的可触达市场非常小,否则那种能在 30 分钟内修复一切的商业,将会摧毁那种需要两天的商业。

speaker: Unknown
zh: 百分之百。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's been the history of technology, right?
zh: 而这一直是技术的历史,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I give the example of like the companies that were not afraid to adopt.
zh: 这就是我举那些不害怕采用新事物的公司例子原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Personal computers that say like, oh, we're going to do this stuff by hand.
zh: 个人电脑,那些说「哦,我们还是要手工做这些事」的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: The companies that were not afraid to adopt the internet early on, the companies that also made it their priority.
zh: 那些不害怕早早采用互联网的公司,还有那些把互联网当作优先事项的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's something really interesting to learn from the history of the internet, which is a lot of companies like the internet, but it's like, okay, I'm going to hire a company.
zh: 所以从互联网的历史里有一些非常值得学习的东西,那就是很多公司喜欢互联网,但就像说,好吧,我要雇一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That does the internet for me.
zh: 替我做互联网的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so many companies in AI.
zh: AI 领域有太多这样的公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still happening, interestingly, right?
zh: 有意思的是,这种事现在还在发生,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so funny because I talk to a lot of enterprises and it's so common that they tell me that they don't own their own website.
zh: 很好笑,因为我跟很多企业聊过,他们告诉我他们并不拥有自己的网站,这太常见了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there is a parallel here, which is that there's going to be the companies that say, I love AI, can we buy a bunch of AI licenses?
zh: 所以这里有一个平行对照:会有那种说「我爱 AI,我们能不能买一堆 AI 许可证」的公司,

speaker: Unknown
en: And throw them to our engineers.
zh: 然后把它们扔给工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's going to be the ones that say, no, no, no, no, this is a disruption that creates a new competitive landscape.
zh: 也会有那种说「不不不不,这是一场颠覆,它创造了一个全新的竞争格局」的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we become really good at mastering this thing, it's a little bit like a redstone.
zh: 如果我们变得非常擅长掌握这个东西,这有点像红石(redstone)。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we become really good at like manipulating this new block, this new raw material, that's going to put us ahead.
zh: 如果我们变得非常擅长操纵这种新方块、这种新原材料,那会让我们领先。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a hundred percent what I believe.
zh: 那是我百分之百相信的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to your point, there is an element of measuring.
zh: 而且正如你所说,这其中有度量的成分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to get only, you know, tactical, like if you improve that metric, that's the end all be all of your business.
zh: 我不想只停留在,你知道的,战术层面,比如如果你改善了那个指标,那就是你业务的终极目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: We like to say that there's iteration speed and there's iteration velocity.
zh: 我们喜欢这么说:有迭代速度(iteration speed),还有迭代速率(iteration velocity)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Iteration speed is, you know, like how quickly you're turning out stuff.
zh: 迭代速度是,你知道的,你产出东西有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why, you know, when I hear about how many tokens you spend, token maxing, and when I hear about how many PRs you land, good for you, good metrics, but velocity implies speed in a direction.
zh: 所以,你知道的,当我听到你花了多少 token、token 最大化(token maxing),当我听到你合入了多少 PR,很好,好指标,但速率意味着带着方向的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could be PRing, PRing, PRing, PRing into oblivion.
zh: 你可能在不停地 PR、PR、PR、PR,一直 PR 到湮灭。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you a very concrete example.
zh: 我给你一个非常具体的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is helping people realize that they can build a lot of things.
zh: AI 正在帮助人们意识到他们可以构建很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I don't know that it's fully helped people realize yet is that there's certain things you should build and there's certain things you should buy.
zh: 而我不确定大家是否已经完全意识到的一点是，有些东西你应该自建，有些东西你应该购买。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's services you can use for certain things and there's things that you should build yourself.
zh: 有些事情你可以用现成的服务来做，有些事情你应该自己构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked to a startup founder recently.
zh: 我最近跟一位初创公司创始人聊过。

speaker: Unknown
en: She came to my office and she was like, yeah, I'm building this really cool idea for agents.
zh: 她来我的办公室，她说，对，我在做一个关于智能体的非常酷的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I thought the idea was really compelling.
zh: 我觉得这个想法非常吸引人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she proceeded to tell me that she was also building her own email service and her own payment gateway.
zh: 然后她接着告诉我，她还在自建自己的邮件服务和自己的支付网关。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of those things might make sense, some of those might not, but like she was taking on a lot.
zh: 其中有些可能合理，有些可能不合理，但她在同时承担很多事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was sort of my sense.
zh: 那大致是我的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, sure, there is the very optimistic take, which is that you can have so many agents working in parallel for you.
zh: 当然，有一个非常乐观的看法，那就是你可以有非常多的智能体为你并行工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: That, yeah, you can take on a lot more projects, but I'm still skeptical because what you really want to do is you want to pick a few set of problems where you think you can have disproportionate alpha and go really deep and spend as many tokens as you can on those problems and move as fast as you can on those problems.
zh: 人们不会尊重那种看起来就像你刚买了个入门套件然后扔到互联网上的原味模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that would imply that vector, that direction that the word velocity implies.
zh: 这就意味着向量、那个方向，也就是“速度”这个词所暗示的含义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not just PR's landed, but where are you headed?
zh: 所以不只是 PR 合入了，而是你朝哪里前进？

speaker: Unknown
en: And are you actually making progress towards your goal?
zh: 你是否真的在朝着你的目标取得进展？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, because if you're doing 20 things at once, you're going to be mediocre in all of them.
zh: 是的，因为如果你同时在做 20 件事，你会在所有这些事情上都很平庸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be successful, you need to build one thing great.
zh: 而要成功，你需要把一件事做到极致。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, this is kind of becoming a thing already.
zh: 顺便说一句，这已经开始成为一个现象了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You realize that a lot of people ship really fast and then you come to their website and it's like a pile of slop.
zh: 你会发现很多人发布得非常快，然后你打开他们的网站，看到的是一堆 slop（垃圾内容）。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can sense that there's no value out over what the model did.
zh: 你能感觉到，在模型产出的基础上没有任何额外的价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, this was already the case with the web.
zh: 顺便说一句，这在网页时代就已经如此了。

speaker: Unknown
en: People would not respect the vanilla template that looked like you just purchased some kind of starter kit and threw it over the internet.
zh: 人们不会尊重那种看起来就像你刚买了一套入门套件然后直接扔到互联网上的原始模板。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think people are really not like, it's almost like you're tuning out a bit when you see something that looks like it was just regurgitated by the LLM because, okay, what is the value add?
zh: 我觉得人们真的不是——几乎可以说，当你看到某个看起来只是被 LLM 反刍出来的东西时，你会稍微调低注意力，因为，好吧，增值在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you could one shot it, I can also one shot it.
zh: 如果你能一把生成出来，我也能一把生成出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's an element there of like, again, the sweating, the details that help you communicate your intent and your values and what you're trying to pursue much better.
zh: 所以这里有一个要素，再次强调，是打磨细节，它能帮你更好地传达你的意图、你的价值观，以及你想要追求的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, if you have multiple $200 subscriptions a month, pay attention because I want to be working closely with a couple of you to build Cloudroom.
zh: 顺便说一句，如果你每个月有多个 200 美元的订阅，请注意，因为我想和你们中的几位紧密合作来构建 Cloudroom。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an open source platform for running agents in the cloud.
zh: 这是一个用于在云端运行智能体的开源平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the world's first open source solution for cloud agents, right?
zh: 这是世界上第一个云端智能体的开源解决方案，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have Devin, you have Cursor, you have Codex, you have Claude.
zh: 你有 Devin，你有 Cursor，你有 Codex，你有 Claude。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these are closed.
zh: 这些全都是闭源的。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want you to use their own subscription, their own harness, their own GUI.
zh: 它们想让你使用它们自己的订阅、它们自己的 harness、它们自己的 GUI。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're already paying for inference.
zh: 但你已经在为推理付费了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're already paying for tokens.
zh: 你已经在为 token 付费了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have probably multiple subscriptions.
zh: 你很可能有多个订阅。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should be able to use that inference.
zh: 你应该能够使用那些推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should be able to use your favorite models, your favorite harness.
zh: 你应该能够使用你最喜欢的模型、你最喜欢的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is Cloudroom.
zh: 这就是 Cloudroom。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fully open source and it's free.
zh: 它完全开源，而且免费。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, right now it's not fully open to the public.
zh: 不过，目前它还没有完全向公众开放。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm looking for the real power users, the people who can give me feedback daily, people with high taste when it comes to coding agents and running agents in the cloud.
zh: 我在寻找真正的重度用户，那些能每天给我反馈的人，那些在编程智能体和在云端运行智能体方面有高品味的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if that's you, if you're paying for a $200 plan on Codex, Claude Code and a bunch of other stuff, go to cloudroom.dev and join the waitlist.

zh: 最坏的情况是你的数据包在互联网上到处被丢弃，最后落在低优先级队列里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a high priority bandwidth system, you're basically taking up space in this very, very expensive backbone that is underneath the ocean in between California and the Netherlands.
zh: 而在一个高优先级带宽系统里，你基本上是占用了一条非常非常昂贵的主干道，它就在加州和荷兰之间的海底。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但如果你也完全一无所知，我觉得你可能会没能把 AI 推得更狠。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if an AI ships that system and I'm hosting it in the Netherlands and I notice that the page is taking like a second to load.
